summary: This note covers Northwestern University's athletic nickname history, its participation in the Chicago Star Partnership with City Colleges, its student-run law journals, its renewable energy and sustainability commitments, and its student media outlets. It mixes university history with descriptions of several scholarly and student publications.
one_line: Overview of Northwestern University's Wildcats nickname, Chicago Star Partnership, sustainability efforts, law reviews, and student publications.
key_facts: Northwestern's football team plays at Ryan Field, formerly known as Dyche Stadium.
Northwestern's basketball, wrestling, and volleyball teams play at Welsh-Ryan Arena.
Before 1924, Northwestern's teams were known as "The Purple" and unofficially as "The Fighting Methodists."
Wallace Abbey, a writer for the Chicago Daily Tribune, bestowed the Wildcats name on the university in 1924.
In 1972, the student body voted to change the official nickname from "Wildcats" to "Purple Haze," but the new name never stuck.
In April 2016, Northwestern announced it signed on to the Chicago Star Partnership, a City Colleges initiative.
Mayor Rahm Emanuel influenced the Chicago Star Partnership, encouraging local universities to increase opportunities for Chicago Public Schools students.
In January 2009, the Green Power Partnership, sponsored by the EPA, listed Northwestern as one of the top 10 universities in the country in purchasing energy from renewable sources.
Northwestern matches 74 million kilowatt hours of its annual energy use with Green-e Certified Renewable Energy Certificates, representing 30 percent of its total annual electricity use.
The 2010 Report by The Sustainable Endowments Institute awarded Northwestern a "B-" on its College Sustainability Report Card.
The Initiative for Sustainability and Energy at Northwestern (ISEN) was launched in 2008.
The Northwestern University Law Review publishes four issues each year and extended its presence onto the web with weekly scholarly pieces on the Colloquy.
The Northwestern Journal of Technology and Intellectual Property's current editor-in-chief is Aisha Lavinier.
The Northwestern Interdisciplinary Law Review was founded in 2008 and is published annually by an editorial board of Northwestern undergraduates.
The Daily Northwestern, established in 1881, is the main student newspaper and is supported wholly by advertisers.
Syllabus, the undergraduate yearbook, was first published in 1885 and is distributed in late May.
